sourceAttempts.family: Paddle SC Broad River trip pages
sourceAttempts.result: The state paddling trail lists twelve suggested trips with named public endpoints, distances, difficulty, access notes, dam/portage warnings and numeric flow or stage cues. Eight direct reaches plus seven contiguous combinations were selected to bring South Carolina to thirty total routes without crossing a dam or inventing a new access point.
Downloaded PaddlePoints116.kml and matched Peake-Alston, Harbison, Ninety-Nine Islands, Daltons, Lockhart, Broad River Landing, Neal Shoals, Sandy, Shelton and Strother coordinates and access notes.
SCDNR documents the 15-mile Ninety-Nine Islands Dam to Pacolet confluence scenic river and public access network. It corroborates the upper corridor's public-river context and dam hazards.
Used direct Broad River telemetry at Alston (02161000), near Carlisle (02156500), and below Ninety-Nine Islands Reservoir (02153551). Paddle SC's published thresholds remain the scoring evidence.
Added separate Wikimedia Commons Broad River photographs for the Columbia and Blacksburg corridors, including public-domain and NOAA-sourced images.
